origin.description: Return the elements of string that match pattern. This is string[str_detect(string, pattern)] after missing matches are dropped, and the same elements as grep with value TRUE.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A plain character vector is a regular expression. fixed compares bytes, and coll uses the locale's collation rules. The empty string and boundary patterns are not allowed.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, return the elements that do not match. Must be a single TRUE or FALSE.

origin.details: A missing detection is treated as not selected, so a missing string is never returned. The subscript is applied to the original string, not to a recycled copy. A true position past the end of string is NA. Names of the retained elements are kept. No matches on a named string is a named empty character vector.
origin.value: A character vector, usually shorter than string.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple")
result <- str_subset(fruit, "b")
writeLines(paste0('str_subset(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "b") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.'))

translation.description: Return the elements of string that match pattern.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Passed to str_detect. A plain string is a regular expression. fixed, coll, and regex select that engine. The empty string and boundary are errors.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, return the elements that do not match.

translation.details: str_detect builds the logical index. Only True selects an element. The values are taken from the original string, so a true index past its length is NA rather than another copy of a length-1 string. Names of the retained elements are kept.
translation.value: A list of strings, usually shorter than string. A selected position past the end is NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.subset import str_subset
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
result = str_subset(fruit, "b")
print('str_subset(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "b") returns ' + ", ".join(result) + '.')
